title: introduce-rag-harness-schematic-templates-and-local-runner
author: Maya Chen
commits:
3 commits: 1) scaffold: add rag-harness directory with schematic template and README
2) feat: add example tool-stubs and prompt sets + devcontainer for local iteration
3) ci/docs: add CI job to run harness smoke tests and publish quickstart page
description:
Motivation: Provide a compact, reproducible RAG test harness and template set for product teams and examples authors to validate agent/tool-calling flows locally and in CI. This PR adds a lightweight 'schematic' template format plus runnable example stubs so engineers can create reproducible regressions for tool integrations and prompt/eval suites. References: Linear ENG-8321, internal testing playbook, and docs site quickstart section (docs link included below).

What this adds (single continuous description): The rag-harness folder contains a human-readable schematic.yaml that defines: - agents: logical agent names, supported tools, and expected tool signatures - flows: staged conversation traces (user -> agent -> tool -> agent) that serve as deterministic smoke tests - assertions: simple output/metadata checks to detect regressions (exact match, regex, and token-frequency heuristics) Alongside the schematic are two example artifacts: - examples/prompt-sets.json: canonical prompts used by CI to exercise common edge cases (context-window boundaries, streaming chunks, tool timeouts) - examples/tool-stubs.ts: a TypeScript dev shim that implements the tools declared in schematic.yaml; it logs call payloads and returns deterministic fixtures to make local runs stable.

Developer experience: Included devcontainer.json and a small runner script (ci/run-integration.sh) so contributors can: 1) Open the folder in VS Code with the devcontainer, 2) run ./scripts/run-harness locally to execute the flows against local Redwood CLI or remote endpoint (configurable via environment), 3) iterate on prompt-sets and tool stubs without spinning up infra. The quickstart page under site/content/quickstarts explains configuration variables, examples for Hosted vs. Private endpoints, and recommended checklist for turning a schematic into a production regression test.

CI and safety: Added a lightweight GitHub Actions job (.github/workflows/harness-ci.yml) that: - boots a matrix for node versions (18/20) - runs the harness runner against a mock endpoint (tool stubs) - lints prompt-sets for banned tokens and verifies assertions pass The job is intentionally fast (~30s per matrix) so it can gate docs/quickstart changes without adding heavy runtime cost. Secrets for hitting real endpoints are opt-in via repository secrets and not required for the fast path.

Checklist (what to review): - [x] schematic.yaml structure and examples cover common agent-tool patterns (sync, async, streaming) - [x] tool-stubs.ts exercises all declared tool signatures - [x] prompt-sets include failure/edge cases (timeouts, long-context) - [x] docs quickstart page clearly documents dev and CI flow - [x] CI workflow runs and passes on the repo (see CI status)

Review notes and conversation (excerpted inline in the PR body as a continuous narrative): Diego: "Can we make the schematic format compact enough to be hand-edited in PR comments? Also: please add an example for function-style tool return (structured JSON)." Maya: "Added a short example in schematic.yaml and expanded tool-stubs to emit structured JSON fixtures. Kept top-level keys minimal so it's easy to paste into issues." Harper: "CI should warn but not fail on flaky streaming checks; mark streaming assertions as advisory." Maya: "Streaming assertions are now opt-in per-flow; CI will emit a warning and continue for advisory checks." Rohan: "Docs page needs a short troubleshooting section for auth/timeouts." Maya: "Added troubleshooting and a short example for switching between hosted and private endpoints using REDWOOD_ENDPOINT env var."

Migration / rollout: This is additive and backwards-compatible: teams can adopt the harness by copying schematic.yaml into their repo, customizing tool stubs, and adding the CI workflow. The quickstart page links to a template PR checklist to help internal adoption.

How to validate locally: 1) git clone && cd redwood-quickstarts/rag-harness 2) code . (open devcontainer) 3) ./scripts/run-harness --schematic schematic.yaml --runner examples/tool-stubs.ts 4) inspect results under _harness-output/ for assertion reports

Release notes: Added a quickstart for an opinionated RAG test harness and schema-driven templates to help teams validate tool-calling and agent regressions locally and in CI.

Links: Docs quickstart draft: https://docs.redwood.ai/quickstarts/rag-harness  Linear: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-8321
release_notes: Introduce an opinionated RAG harness + schematic templates for local and CI-driven agent/tool regression testing; includes devcontainer, examples, and fast CI job for docs gating.
notes: PR merged with squash. Minor follow-ups planned: a Python runner, and a prebuilt mock service image to make CI even faster.
